title: The Boy Who Collected Stars
summary: A boy who keeps a nightly journal of the stars and constellations he observes from his rooftop ends up helping his school identify a newly visible comet.
poll: Keeping a careful record of something every day, even when nothing exciting happens, is a waste of time.

versions.title: The Boy Who Collected Stars
versions.text:
Tariq lives in a big city. He loves the night sky. Each night, he climbs up to the roof.

He takes a journal with him. He looks up at the stars. He draws what he sees. He writes the date too.

He does this night after night. He names the stars he sees. He draws them in the book. The book fills up with pages.

One night, Tariq sees something new. It is a small light. He has not drawn it before. He shows the book to his teacher.

His teacher looks at the pages. She sees many good notes. She tells the school about it. The school calls a star group.

The star group looks at the sky too. They say it is a comet! Tariq's notes helped them see it. Now Tariq is a young star watcher.

versions.title: The Boy Who Collected Stars
versions.text:
Tariq lives in a big city near the desert. He loves to watch the night sky. Each night, he climbs up to his roof.

He takes his journal with him. He looks up at the many stars. He draws the shapes he sees. He writes the date in his book too.

He does this night after night, for many months. He names the stars and shapes he finds. He draws them all in his journal. His journal slowly fills up with pages.

One night, Tariq notices something new in the sky. It is a small, fuzzy point of light. He has never drawn anything like it before. He shows his journal to his teacher the next day.

His teacher looks closely at all the pages. She sees many careful notes and drawings. She tells the school about what Tariq found. The school then calls a star club for help.

The star club looks at the sky too. They say it is a real comet! Tariq's careful notes helped them find it. Now Tariq is known as a young star watcher.

He carries his journal with him every time he goes up there to watch the sky, searching for familiar constellations among the countless stars scattered overhead. He draws the patterns he notices in careful, consistent lines, taking his time with every detail, and he records the exact date and time at the top of each page.

He keeps doing this night after night, for many months in a row, rarely missing a clear evening, gradually learning something new each time he looks up. He gives careful names to the constellations and patterns he finds, and he draws every single one of them in his journal, no matter how faint. Little by little, his journal fills with pages of meticulous, patient records.

One night, Tariq notices an unfamiliar phenomenon sitting quietly in the sky above him, a small, fuzzy point of light that he simply does not recognize. He checks through his old records, but he has never drawn anything quite like it before, so the next morning he excitedly shows his journal to his teacher at school.

His teacher looks closely through all of his careful pages, genuinely impressed by months of consistent observations and detailed sketches, and she tells the school principal about what Tariq has discovered. The school then contacts a real astronomy club for expert help with the unusual sighting.

The astronomy club studies the night sky through a powerful telescope that very evening, and they confirm that the strange light is in fact a newly visible comet. Tariq's meticulous records helped the club confirm it much more quickly than they expected. Now Tariq is known throughout town as a dedicated young astronomer.

versions.title: The Boy Who Collected Stars
versions.text:
Tariq lives in a city on the edge of the desert, where the night sky is usually remarkably clear and brilliantly full of countless stars, and he has dreamed of becoming a professional astronomer since he was quite young. Each clear night, without exception, he climbs up to the roof of his house with his journal in hand, ready to begin another session of careful, meticulous observations.

He carries his journal with him every time he ascends to watch the sky, searching patiently for familiar constellations scattered among the countless stars overhead. He draws the patterns he notices in careful, remarkably consistent lines, taking his time with every single detail, and he conscientiously records the exact date and time at the top of each page he fills.

He continues doing this night after night, for many consecutive months, rarely missing even a single clear evening, gradually learning something valuable each time he looks up at the sky above him. He assigns careful names to the constellations and patterns he discovers, and he draws every single one of them in his journal, regardless of how faint or distant it appears. Little by little, his journal accumulates pages upon pages of meticulous, remarkably patient records.

One night, Tariq notices an unfamiliar phenomenon sitting quietly in the sky above him, a small, fuzzy point of light that he simply does not recognize at all, despite his many months of careful, dedicated practice. He checks thoroughly through his extensive old records, but he has never drawn anything quite like it before, so the next morning he excitedly presents his journal to his teacher at school.

His teacher looks closely through all of his meticulous pages, genuinely impressed by months of consistent observations and remarkably detailed sketches recorded with evident patience and skill. She informs the school principal about what Tariq has discovered, and the school subsequently contacts a reputable astronomy club for expert assistance with the unusual sighting.

The astronomy club examines the night sky through a powerful telescope that very same evening, and they confirm that the strange light is in fact a newly visible comet passing through the region for the first time in many years. Tariq's meticulous records helped the club confirm the discovery considerably more quickly than they otherwise would have managed.

The experience teaches Tariq a lasting lesson about patience and consistency: by observing the sky carefully every single night, without ever expecting anything extraordinary to occur, he became the one person whose records made an unexpected discovery possible, a lesson that remains with him well beyond that single remarkable evening.

MID.prompt: Explain how Tariq's habits as a careful observer helped lead to the discovery of the comet. Use at least two details from the story.
checklist: I explained how Tariq's habits led to the discovery.
I used at least two details from the story.
I organized my ideas in a clear order.
MID.modelAnswer: Tariq's careful habits played a big part in the discovery of the comet. Every clear night for many months, he climbed to his roof and recorded the date, time, and the constellations he saw in his journal. Because he kept such detailed records, he could tell right away that a new, unfamiliar light in the sky did not match anything he had drawn before. His teacher and the astronomy club trusted his careful observations, which helped them confirm the comet quickly.

HIGH.prompt: The poll says keeping a careful record of something every day, even when nothing exciting happens, is a waste of time. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about Tariq's journal and the comet.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I disagree that keeping a careful daily record is a waste of time. For months, Tariq recorded the sky in his journal even though most nights seemed ordinary, with no exciting discovery at all. That consistency is exactly what let him recognize the unfamiliar phenomenon when it finally appeared, since his meticulous records showed he had never drawn anything like it before. Someone might argue that most of his nightly entries led to nothing special, but without that patient, unglamorous habit, Tariq would never have noticed the comet or helped the astronomy club confirm it.
